newsitem.title: ETHIOPIA: Ethiopia blast kills one, wounds Britons and French.
newsitem.headline: Ethiopia blast kills one, wounds Britons and French.

text.p: At least one person was killed and four Britons and two French citizens were among 42 wounded in grenade blasts in the Ethiopian capital on Saturday night, diplomats and state radio reported on Sunday.

"I can confirm that four British people and two French people were injured by a grenade attack at the Blue Tops restaurant," the British consul in Addis Ababa, Florence Napthen, told Reuters by telephone.
"The two British men were reasonably seriously injured, mostly from flying glass. But their wives are not too bad and none of their lives is in danger," Napthen said.

Ethiopian radio said at least one person was killed and 42 injured when grenades were lobbed into the Tigray hotel, in the Piazza area of the city centre, and Blue Tops, an Italian restaurant which is a favourite haunt of wealthy Ethiopians and foreigners.
Unconfirmed reports said there were two other blasts on Saturday night in the capital.
Police sealed off the restaurant and hotel on Sunday and journalists were denied entry to the Black Lion hospital where two of the wounded Britons were being treated.
Napthen said one or more unidentified assailants threw the grenade into the Blue Tops at about 7.30 p.m. (1630 GMT) on Saturday before the restaurant was at its busiest.
She declined to release the names of the British casualties but said they were residents not tourists.
The French embassy was not immediately available for comment.
State radio, quoting police officials, said one person was killed and 34 wounded at the Tigray hotel.
The report did not say if any suspects had been arrested.

Several bombs have exploded in Addis and provincial cities in the past year and last November an Ethiopian Airlines plane was hijacked and crashed into the sea off the Comoro Islands, killing some 125 people on board.
